metas.name: The Act of Killing
metas.description: Captures impunity as performance. Indonesian mass killers, never punished and locally celebrated, gleefully re-stage their killings as Hollywood genres, until one man's body reacts before his conscience does.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description: Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

metas.name: The Death of Stalin
metas.description: Captures absolute power as petty, terrified men improvising. Stalin drops dead and his inner circle plot, flatter and panic in the same breath — very funny, and people keep being shot between jokes.

metas.name: Lawrence of Arabia
metas.description: Captures a man inventing himself at desert scale. Nearly four hours: the landscape is a character, and so is the gap between the legend being built and the person inside it.

metas.name: Summer of Soul
metas.description: Captures a community's archive left in a basement for 50 years. The 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival — Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Mahalia Jackson, Sly Stone — in footage almost nobody saw.

metas.name: 20 Feet from Stardom
metas.description: Captures the voices you know best belonging to people you can't name. Backup singers for the Stones, Springsteen and Sting — huge talent, a career spent three steps behind someone else.

metas.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
metas.description: Captures celebrity worship in 1882. A famous outlaw ageing and paranoid, and a young admirer who memorised his life from dime novels and moves into his orbit — slow, golden, narrated like a history book.

metas.name: Apollo 13
metas.description: Captures competence under constraint. An explosion in space, and the film becomes people in rooms with slide rules solving the next physical problem before the air runs out — the opposite of lone-hero cinema.

metas.name: First Man
metas.description: Captures the Moon landing from inside a grieving, taciturn man. Armstrong as an engineer who can land anything except in his own family's pain; the flights are rattling, cramped and procedural.

metas.name: When We Were Kings
metas.description: Captures Ali as a political and verbal artist at his peak. The Rumble in the Jungle, Zaire 1974: training footage, a music festival, Mobutu's stadium, and Ali talking everyone, including himself, into belief.

metas.name: All the President's Men
metas.description: Captures journalism as shoe leather. Watergate as phone calls, parking garages, notebooks and editors asking 'what else do you have?' — verification repeated until a presidency moves.

metas.name: Spotlight
metas.description: Captures an investigation as a team slowly realising the size of the room they're in. Boston Globe reporters, church abuse, sealed records, survivors telling it plainly — no heroics beyond persistence.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description: Captures obsession with a case that will not close. San Francisco, years of codes, files, basements and false certainties; the killer fades and the men who chased him are what's left damaged.

metas.name: Silence
metas.description: Captures faith tested by other people's suffering, not your own. Jesuit priests in 17th-century Japan, where Christians are tortured to make them apostatise and God does not answer — Scorsese's quietest, most unresolved film.
